newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: France arrests Guiana independence leader.
newsitem.headline: France arrests Guiana independence leader.

text.p: French police arrested a leading member of French Guiana's independence movement, local state-owned radio said on Saturday.

The radio said Alain Michel and several other members of the Guiana National Progressive Party (PNPG) were arrested on Friday in French Guiana's capital Cayenne and were transported on Saturday to the French Caribbean island of Martinique aboard a military aircraft.

Police declined to comment on why Michel was arrested. Officials close to the PNPG said the arrest stemmed from an attack on the home of French Guiana's state prosecutor during riots that shook the French overseas department last November.

French Guiana, on the northeast coast of South America, is the only non-independent territory on the mainland of the Western Hemisphere. Its economy is heavily dependent on subsidies from mainland France and 23 percent of the population of 150,000 is unemployed.
The PNPG favours independence from mainland France.
The European Space Agency (ESA) Ariane rocket launch site is located in Kourou, French Guiana, 72 km (50 miles) from Cayenne.
